Welcome to Parkfield Primary School
A two-form entry primary school with nursery provision, located in large, beautiful grounds in the West Hendon area, with excellent transport links.
We are proud members of The Elliot Foundation Academies Trust (TEFAT).

Values and Ethos
At Parkfield Primary School, we believe that all children are entitled to a broad and balanced curriculum which is interesting, engaging and provides a range of learning opportunities that help develop their life-long learning.
Our curriculum is planned to ensure that every child has the opportunity to develop:​
socially, emotionally, intellectually, physically, spiritually, morally and culturally
positive attitudes, healthy relationships, and essential life and work skills
the ability to make informed choices, gaining experiences and developing a sense of responsibility.
We will strive to motivate and excite the children, making them active partners in their own learning to ensure we are all Achieving Together.
Parkfield Values

Welcome
It gives me great pleasure to welcome you to Parkfield Primary School.
We are a large primary school with a nursery, ranging from 2-11 year olds, located in West Hendon housing ample grounds for children to learn and play throughout their school day.
Alongside over 30 other national primary schools, including a local cluster, we are proud members of The Elliot Foundation Academies Trust (TEFAT).
Welcoming pupils from all over the world, we are proud of our thriving and diverse community in which we share the motto of 'Achieving Together'.

Wraparound Care
Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club opens at 7.45am daily for pupils in Reception to Year 6. The children will be safely cared for whilst enjoying a nutritious breakfast and an active start to the day.
The children have a choice at breakfast and they have opportunities to do art, creative activities and sports.
The cost is £4.00 per child, per day, and is booked via Arbor.
Breakfast club is also available to our youngest children who attend both our 2-year-olds' nursery (Apples and Pears) and our 3-year-olds' nursery (Cherries).
There are different charges because of the extra staffing required for such young children. Please ask about this at the office.
Super Star Sport
Click here for the Booking Portal - scroll down to select the Parkfield Primary school options.
After School Provision, run by Super Star Sport, is from 3.20-6pm, daily.
Pricing is matched to the available finish times of: 4.20pm, 4.45pm or 6pm.
Bookings are made through the Pebble booking portal - link above.
Parents are able to use childcare vouchers as payment.

Reading
Parkfield's famous Library
As part our venture to ensure all children find enjoyment in reading, we have an amazing library in our school. Run by our fabulous librarian, Mrs Dennehy, the children love going to the library weekly to choose a book for home. And with over 1,000 beautiful books to choose from, this is not always an easy task!
Teaching of Reading at Parkfield
Reading Lessons - EYFS - Year 2
Daily Carousel Reading Sessions
Children in Years EYFS - Year 2 participate in daily reading sessions of 30 minutes each following the guidelines of Little Wandle. Set up in a carousel style, the children will rotate between 5 different reading activities. Three of these sessions will be a Guided Reading Session with the Class Teacher or Support Staff. The other activities will be linked to the phonics sounds they have learnt or be a follow up activity to the book they have read in the guided sessions. There will also be a Reading for Pleasure session where children will have a chance to read a book from the Classroom Library or from a box of books linked to the topic provided by Barnet Library Service.
Reading Lessons Year 2 - 6
Whole Class Reading Sessions
Years 5 and 6 complete reading sessions, as a whole class. Based off a high-quality and challenging texts, the students will do a range of reading including independent reading, listening to reading modelled, paired reading and choral reading. All of the students will have access to the same activities and levels of questioning and will be led in a discussion to help pupils get to grips with new vocabulary and develop their understanding of the text. Depending on the activity, pupils may work in mixed-ability groups, pairs or by themselves.
Once a week, we also do an independent comprehension session. In this session, children will practice the a range of comprehension skills independently and work on using the text to support their responses.
Accelerated Reader - Home Reading Books
Accelerated Reader is a computer program that will help to develop children’s independent reading. It works in quite a simple way; the child will pick a book at their own level, and when finished will take a short quiz on the computer. The quiz is a key feature of how we change home reading books at school for Years 2-6, but is a really important step because if they can pass a quiz about what they have read then this tells us that they have fully understood the content of their book.
All children have undertaken a short reading test that has assigned them a reading band (or Z.P.D.). They are then able to select a book from our library that falls within their Z.P.D. This reading band guides children towards choosing books at an appropriate reading level that are challenging without being frustrating. The aim is for them to pass the quiz and be successful.
All of our home reading books in school have been labelled and put into colour bands that will help with choosing appropriate books. One of the best parts about using Accelerated Reader is that the children can choose their own books to read, rather than having one assigned to them. This in turn, makes reading a much more enjoyable experience as they can choose books that are interesting to them.
Reading for Pleasure

Religious Education
Information to make parents and carers aware they have the right to withdraw:
Religious Education (RE)
Parents and carers have the right to request that their child is withdrawn from all or part of RE. However, we regard RE as an integral part of our curriculum and an important way for children to learn about different beliefs and cultures.
During 1 or 2 of the lessons in Years 4, 5 and 6, parents have the right to request to withdraw their child from the small non-statutory, Sex Education elements of the lesson. These will be the lessons on human reproduction. You are unable to withdraw your child from any lessons within Relationship or Health Education (this includes puberty and menstruation).

Sustainability and Green Curriculum
Barnet School Charter for Sustainability
Parkfield has joined the Barnet School Charter and has committed to:
joining the journey to becoming one of London’s most sustainable boroughs
developing our own Climate Action Plan
starting our journey to becoming more sustainable
The Barnet School Charter is a joint commitment between Parkfield Primary School and Barnet Council:
to work together to empower schools in becoming more sustainable
to work together to contribute to Barnet’s ambitions of becoming a net zero borough by 2042.

New Starters
Welcome to Parkfield! We are so excited to have you join our school community.
This section is designed to be your quick, go-to guide for everything you need to know to hit the ground running. From getting familiar with our uniform to understanding how to order from our delicious meal options, you'll find all the essential information right here. We've also included details on our school values and how to book for our wraparound care options.
We're here to help you every step of the way, ensuring a smooth and successful start at Parkfield!

Keeping Children Safe
TEFAT Safeguarding Policies
For all safeguarding concerns or queries, please contact: safeguarding@parkfieldprimary.org
Are you worried about a child?
If a child is at immediate risk of harm or an emergency situation call 999 immediately.

Newsletters
A fortnightly newsletter is emailed home to all parents. This includes a roundup of news across the school, as well as important dates and updates. If you do not receive these, please ensure the school office has the correct email address for you.
Previous newsletters can be found below.

Pupil Premium
All children in Reception-Year 6 get a lunch at school at no cost, funded by the government and Mayor of London.
We are encouraging all families to register for means-tested free school meals.
If a child receives means-tested FSM, Parkfield receives additional funding through the Pupil Premium. This extra funding is used for various purposes, such as: providing targeted support for disadvantaged children, investing in teacher development and funding enrichment activities.
If your child is eligible for free school meals, they’ll also qualify for the Holiday Activity and Food Programme. Food vouchers may also be available through the Household Support Fund.
